LEFT/FULL/RIGHT lateral UNNEST and non-true join predicates remain rejected with document_sql_unsupported_join. Alternate scalar projection is admitted when the correlation field is declared unique; nullable unique correlations are admitted only for LEFT JOIN LATERAL and null or missing outer correlation values produce no branch row and null lateral projections. Default JOIN LATERAL and CROSS JOIN LATERAL mapped-view subqueries are admitted only with non-null correlation proof, so native document output matches SQL row-dropping semantics. Branch ORDER BY is admitted for deterministic shapes where ordering cannot change row identity, and for non-unique alternate projection when any order key is unique and a bounded branch-row lookup can select the same row deterministically by sorting the full branch order list; compound branch ordering has coverage for both leading-unique and later-unique key order. The bounded lookup rejects candidate-cap overflow with document_sql_bounded_scan_row_cap_exceeded. Branch-only scalar residual predicates are admitted with unique correlation proof and SQL-compatible left null-extension or inner/cross row dropping, and with non-unique echo-field projection through a native LIMIT 1 branch-existence lookup. Source-relative residual predicates are admitted for unique-correlation shapes and for non-unique echo-field projection through the same branch-existence lookup, then evaluated before lateral projection/nulling. Non-unique alternate scalar projection is admitted through branch-row lookup when a branch predicate pins the projected field to one exact value, making duplicate branch identity and branch ordering result-value independent, or when unique order-key proof selects one branch row through a bounded local sort. Broader correlated lateral mapped-view subqueries fail closed with document_sql_lateral_requires_native_producer unless they have a proven native producer contract; document corpus and public SQL diagnostics cover order-sensitive non-unique alternate projection, compound ordering without a unique order key, expression branch ordering, mixed residual/order alternate projection, and relational-fallback rejection.
